subject: Priv infra: conditional operator access and escrow-lite evidence options (MSA/Order Form redlines)
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <contracts@medsyshealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com, security_ops@medsys.health
Date: 2025-08-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment evidence / operator access options

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this — MedSys is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC deployment) for a pilot in Q4. Our compliance team has two core asks we need to lock in before procurement:

1) Evidence/escrow: we need a defensible path to recover a validated snapshot of the runtime and model artifacts in the event of vendor insolvency or contract termination.
2) Operator access: we cannot accept unrestricted vendor operator credentials inside our environment. We need a narrow, auditable option for witnessing or validating a snapshot without persistent key handover.

I attached our current evidence request (MedSys_Evidence_Request_v1.pdf) that outlines the artifacts and the audit windows.

Questions for you: do you have a short list of standard options Redwood offers (sealed snapshot to third-party escrow, remote witnessing, HSM-backed attestation, etc.) and any suggested MSA/Order Form language so our legal team can start a redline pass? Also please include rough timelines for producing artifacts and typical lead times for a witness session.

Happy to set a 30-min sync this week — procurement@medsyshealth.com is copied.

Best,
Jordan Miles
Director, Contracts
MedSys Health

Attachment: MedSys_Evidence_Request_v1.pdf

From: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <contracts@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-08-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence / operator access options

Jordan — thanks, and appreciated the clear ask. We have two pragmatic patterns customers use; I'll summarize and attach a short playbook.

Option A — Sealed snapshot (third-party escrow):
- Redwood produces a read-only snapshot of the on-prem/VPC runtime (binaries, model weights, runbook & manifest). Snapshot is sealed and deposited with a mutually agreed escrow agent.
- Access triggers: explicit contract termination or independent escrow release criteria.
- Pros: aligns with traditional escrow expectations.
- Cons: set-up time for escrow agent; transfer logistics and notarization.

Option B — Attested witness + temporary console session (preferred by many regulated customers):
- Redwood performs a witness session with customer reps where we produce a sealed digest + HSM attestation and allow a time-bound remote console view (no persistent operator keys). Session can be recorded and signed into an Exhibit.
- Pros: faster, avoids permanent key handover; easier for on-call and DR tests.
- Cons: requires defined audit window and scope in the Order Form.

MSA/Order Form language we recommend (high level):
- Define "Operator Access" narrowly: "time-bound, logged, supervise-only console sessions for the purpose of witnessing or remediating incidents; no persistent credentials or keys are provided."
- Add an "Evidence & Escrow Exhibit" that enumerates artifacts, responsible party, transfer triggers, and attestation options (sealed snapshot vs attested witness).
- Carveouts for SLA and support: clear runbook delivery timelines (e.g., 5-10 business days for snapshot preparation) and any one-time fees.

I've attached a short playbook (Redwood_PrivDeploy_Playbook.pdf) and proposed rollout timeline. For legal redlines, I'll loop David (legal) and Laura (ops) — David, can you outline the MSA/Exhibit language we should propose as a starting point?

Call? I can do 8/11 or 8/12 afternoon PT.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Customer Security & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_PrivDeploy_Playbook.pdf

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2025-08-10T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence / operator access options — legal sketch

Neha — quick sketch from legal for the MSA redline and exhibit approach. High-level points to propose to MedSys:

1) Definitions: add a defined term "Controlled Witnessing" and "Sealed Snapshot" to the MSA. Controlled Witnessing = a time-limited session, recorded, with attestation artifacts; Sealed Snapshot = read-only artifact placed with a mutually agreed escrow agent or retained by Redwood under sealed custody pending release triggers.

2) No permanent key transfer: prohibit transfer of vendor private keys or management credentials except as expressly permitted for one-off disaster recovery with explicit customer authorization and written witness statement.

3) Audit window: default 48 hours for witness sessions; customers can request up to 7 days with a documented justification and additional fees.

4) Exhibit X (Evidence & Escrow):
- Lists deliverables (runtime manifest, model checksum, container images, runbook, operator-playbook).
- Includes required attestation format (HSM-signed digest + notarized chain).
- Specifies retention and access triggers.

5) Order Form fields: add checkboxes for (a) Escrow Agent vs Attested Witness, (b) Desired audit-window length, (c) Fees and timeline.

Operational note: Redwood prefers attested witness where possible to avoid prolonged escrow logistics. If customer insists on third-party escrow, we can support but will need time to onboard the agent and run a signed handoff.

I'm attaching the current redline (Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx) for Neha's markups. Neha — please advise if MedSys is likely to accept attestation in lieu of escrow (Jordan?), and we'll prepare a tailored Exhibit and Order Form language.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx

From: Jordan Miles <contracts@medsyshealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com, security_ops@medsys.health
Date: 2025-08-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment evidence / operator access options

Neha, David — thanks for the clear options and the preliminary redline. We spoke with compliance this morning: our preference is still to have a sealed snapshot with a neutral escrow agent (legal risk committee is conservative).

That said, we are open to a hybrid approach: Redwood prepares a sealed snapshot and concurrently conducts an attested witness session so we can validate artifacts more quickly while escrow logistics are completed. Two asks from our side:

- Order Form must include explicit data residency language (US-only hosting) and the audit-window selection field you mentioned.
- We will need the Exhibit to include a list of required artifacts (same as your list) plus a requirement for transfer acceptance testing steps.

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to finalize the order form and MSA amendments by 8/29 to start a Sept pilot. Procurement contact is procurement@medsyshealth.com — they will push a PO once redlines are acceptable.

I'll set up a 30-min call for 8/14 09:00 PT to review the draft Exhibit and Order Form additions. Attaching an updated evidence request with clarifications (MedSys_Evidence_Request_v1.1.pdf).

Jordan Miles
Director, Contracts
MedSys Health

Attachment: MedSys_Evidence_Request_v1.1.pdf
